match.reason: The closest bank point, ecb-ways-invest, covers shares, property, managed funds, super and term deposits, but it does not teach bonds, and adding a card on bonds is more than a small change.

draft.title: Types of investments
card: Money kept in an account at a bank or similar institution, which pays interest. A term deposit locks the money away for a set time.
A share is a small part of ownership in a company. Investors may earn dividends (a share of profit) or gain if the share price rises.
Land or buildings, such as a house or a shop. Investors may earn rent or gain if the property's value rises.

A bond is a loan to a government or company that pays interest. A managed fund pools many people's money, and professionals invest it. Superannuation is money saved during working life for retirement, and it is often invested in shares, property and bonds.
draft.remember: Investments differ in what you own or lend: a deposit, a company share, property, a bond, a pooled fund or retirement savings.

a.q: Tom buys a share in an Australian company. What does he now own?
opts: A small part of the company
A loan the company must repay him
A fixed term of interest payments
A part of a pool of properties
a.why: A share is part ownership of a company, so Tom owns a small part of it. A loan to a company that pays interest is a bond, not a share.
a.clue: Think about owning part of a business, not lending to it.

b.q: Priya lends money to the government and is paid regular interest. Which investment is this?
b.why: A bond is a loan to a government or company that pays interest. A share is tempting because it can also pay money, but a share is part ownership of a company, not a loan.
b.clue: Priya is a lender, not an owner.

a.best: A small part of the company
